You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control
input.rationale: The agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data return/export right for us. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) is entirely one-directional: licenses cease and Licensee must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information to Licensor within five days, with officer certification; nothing requires Licensor to return or export Licensee's data or to assist with migration off the hosted trading platform. Searches for "transition", "return"/"export" and data-related terms show nothing elsewhere: Article XX and Articles XXII–XXIII address change-of-control termination, right of first refusal and remedies, and the General Provisions (p0145–p0159) contain no wind-down provision. The confidentiality return-of-materials language likewise binds only Licensee. This falls below the fallback (90 days of assistance plus 30-day data export) and, absent any data-return right at all, sits close to walk-away territory. We propose inserting a new Article XXI(c) at the preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter, with survival; 90 days of assistance is offered as a fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to hand everything back but says nothing about getting our own data back or moving off the platform, so we have added a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph: up to six months of assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, export of Licensee Data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept 90 days of assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: (c) TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all data, records and trade and account information of Licensee and its customers stored in or processed by the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data") in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Licensee in writing. This Section shall survive termination of this Agreement.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data return/export right for us. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) is entirely one-directional: licenses cease and Licensee must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information to Licensor within five days, with officer certification; nothing requires Licensor to return or export Licensee's data or to assist with migration off the hosted trading platform. Searches for "transition", "return"/"export" and data-related terms show nothing elsewhere: Article XX and Articles XXII–XXIII address change-of-control termination, right of first refusal and remedies, and the General Provisions (p0145–p0159) contain no wind-down provision. The confidentiality return-of-materials language likewise binds only Licensee. This falls below the fallback (90 days of assistance plus 30-day data export) and, absent any data-return right at all, sits close to walk-away territory. We propose inserting a new Article XXI(c) at the preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of Licensee Data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter, with survival; 90 days of assistance is offered as a fallback in the comment.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay floor, shortfall charge, or volume cap on our usage:

- **Usage-only pricing:** The fee table (p0056–p0063) begins at a 0–10 US$bn band, and p0070 calculates each month's fee from actual Monthly Notional Volume. Zero trading in a month yields zero user fee.
- **Fixed fees are for ordered services:** The only recurring fixed charge is US$2,500/month for Technical Support Services (p0086) — payment for an ordered service, which the preferred position expressly permits.
- **Supplemental Payments (p0078)** are a 33% share of amounts we actually earn from third parties, not a committed spend; the Rebate Shares mechanic (p0076) runs in our favour.

This sits at the **preferred** position, so no edit is warranted. Noted in the rationale (not flagged here) is the 36-month Initial Period with renewal at Licensor's option and no Licensee termination-for-convenience right (p0049) — a term/termination issue for the relevant rule, which creates no take-or-pay exposure given the absence of any volume floor.

**Finding submitted: DEVIATION (WARRANTY)**

**What the document does.** Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS," all warranties "WHETHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED" are disclaimed (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, completeness, accuracy, title), and Licensor expressly does not warrant error-free or uninterrupted operation, or that nonconformity to the Documentation can or will be corrected.

**Why it fails.** There is no affirmative performance or conformance warranty anywhere in the agreement. The nearest thing — Article VII(f) Error Corrections — only obliges Licensor to use "commercially reasonable efforts," which is a support undertaking, not a warranty, and gives us no repair, replace or refund remedy. This is squarely the playbook's walk-away position and does not reach even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).

**Redline (validated, ok:true).**
1. `p0110` — open the disclaimer with "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH BELOW IN THIS ARTICLE," so the disclaimer no longer swallows the warranty.
2. Insert after `p0116` — an express warranty: professional and workmanlike services; 12-month conformance of the Licensed Technology to the Documentation and Specifications; no malicious code; compliance with applicable laws; with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund of fees paid as the remedy.

The comment flags the 90/30-day fallback as an acceptable landing zone if the Licensor pushes back on the 12-month period.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review — findings and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. Of the nineteen rules assessed, seven clauses are compliant and require no action, eight are deviations requiring redlines, and four rules are unaddressed in the document (insurance, termination for convenience, and post-termination transition assistance / data return).

The Agreement is materially one-sided in the Licensor's favour on the ri[REDACTED] core. Four issues sit in what our playbook treats as walk-away territory and should drive the negotiation:

- **Warranties.** The Licensed Technology is supplied wholly "AS IS" with all express and implied warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty or remedy. The only performance undertaking is a "commercially reasonable efforts" Error Correction obligation in Article VII(f), which is a support commitment rather than a warranty.
- **Indemnities.** The sole indemnity runs from us to the Licensor, and Article XIII expressly excludes all Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims arising from our use of the platform.
- **Limitation of liability.** The cap and the consequential-damages exclusion protect the Licensor only, leaving our liability unlimited and exposed under the broad Article XII indemnity; the Licensor's own cap is set at one half of amounts paid, below our walk-away floor, with no carve-outs.
- **Assignment and change of control.** A blanket one-way ban on our assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, compounded by automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our change of control unless the Licensor consents, with the Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever it believes its interests may be affected.

Secondary but significant: the licence grant excludes our Affiliates and contractors; the Licensor may unilaterally extend the term by a further seven years at its sole option; we have no termination-for-convenience right in a 36-month term; bespoke deliverables we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in the Licensor; and there is no data-return or migration right on exit.

Helpfully, there is **no** exclusivity, no MFN, no minimum volume commitment, no liquidated damages or shortfall charge, and no non-compete binding us. Governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York courts, no arbitration) are at our preferred position.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions, cl. I |
| 2 | High | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions, cl. I |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation |
| 5 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions |
| 6 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | General Provisions |
| 7 | Medium | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation |
| 8 | Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions |
| 10 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions, cl. I |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions, cl. I |
| 12 | Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | Art. IV.I |
| 13 | Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions, cl. I |
| 14 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) |
| 15 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § II, cl. IV(b) (volume-band / fee schedule) |
| 16 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | General Provisions |
| 17 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions / Art. IV |
| 18 | Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (cf. Art. XXI) |

---

## 3. Detail on the deviations and gaps

### High severity

**Licence grant scope (deviation).** The Article II grant runs to the Licensee alone, and restriction (e) bars use or access by any individuals other than employees of the Licensee. Affiliates are defined in cl. 1.1 but never brought within the grant, and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded outright; the only route to add them is the Licensor's discretionary prior written consent, which is not the fallback's "affiliates covered on written notice". Our redline extends the grant and restriction (e) to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, with Licensee responsible for their compliance. We note, without separately flagging, that the licence is not revocable at will and that M&A transfer is partially addressed through the Change of Control provision, where consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

**Warranty (deviation).** Article VIX supplies the platform "AS IS" and disclaims all warranties whether express or implied, including merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, accuracy and title, and expressly negates any commitment that errors or non-conformity to the Documentation will be corrected. This is the rule's walk-away position and falls short of even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). We insert a professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, a 12-month conformance-to-Documentation warranty, no-malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranties, and a repair/replace/refund remedy, carved out of the disclaimer. **Fallback offered in comment:** 90-day services / 30-day deliverable warranty.

### Medium severity

**Assignment and change of control (deviation).** One-way blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment, no affiliate or M&A carve-out, no reasonableness standard, and no corresponding restriction on the Licensor. Article XX compounds this with automatic termination of the Agreement and all our licences on our Change of Control absent prior Licensor consent, with the Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever it believes its interests may be adversely affected. Our redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, makes consent mutual and not unreasonably withheld, bars Licensor assignment to our competitor, and removes the change-of-control termination trigger while retaining notice to the Licensor and the existing definition.

**Vendor indemnity (deviation).** Article XII runs one way only — we indemnify the Licensor for exercise of the licence, the conduct of our business and any breach — and Article XIII excludes all Licensor liability for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party IP. Our redline adds a Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with standard procedure and remedies, disapplies the Article XIII carve-out for that indemnity, and narrows our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our breach of law or material breach. **Fallback offered:** usual exclusions with a 3x annual fees super-cap.

**Limitation of liability (deviation).** Article XIII is entirely one-way: both the consequential-damages exclusion and the cap protect the Licensor only, leaving our liability unlimited and exposed under Article XII. The Licensor's cap of one half of amounts paid is below the walk-away floor, and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Our redline makes the exclusion and cap mutual, sets the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, makes Excluded Claims uncapped, and places payment obligations outside the cap. We also note (not separately flagged) the sweeping sentence in (a) disclaiming all Licensor IP-infringement liability.

### Low severity

**Renewal (deviation).** Article IV.I lets the Licensor unilaterally extend the licence for a further seven years at its sole option, with no opt-out for us and no cap on renewal pricing — worse than the fallback and inconsistent with Articles IV.II and IV.III, which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. Redline: 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

**IP ownership (deviation).** Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights in the Licensor, and the definitions of "Intellectual Property Rights" and "Derivative Work" are broad enough that the bespoke client front end and enhancements we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) fall on the Licensor's side. Our only counter-right is a term-limited, non-sublicensable, non-modifiable Field-of-Use licence that ends on termination with all materials returned. There is also no statement that we retain our own trade, order and market data. We do not disturb the Licensor's ownership of its underlying platform; we insert the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense paid-for Article VII(b) deliverables) plus an express Licensee Data ownership sentence.

**Non-solicitation (deviation).** Article X(b) binds only us, for the Term plus three years, and covers every person employed by the Licensor and its Affiliates. Both the 36-month tail and the all-personnel scope fall in the walk-away band. The general-advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs are already present, so the minimal fix is to make the clause mutual, limit it to individuals directly involved in performance, and cut the tail to 12 months from the end of that involvement.

**Audit (deviation).** Cost allocation is already at our preferred position (Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found), the auditor must be a mutually agreed independent CPA, scope is limited to accounting records, and there is no system-access language. The single failure is the absence of any frequency cap, allowing repeated audits on demand. The 30-day window to permit an audit functions as adequate notice. Redline: once per 12 months, off-site during business hours, confidentiality-bound independent auditor, no access to our systems.

**Vendor insurance (missing).** No insurance obligation on the Licensor anywhere; the only reference to "insurance" is a Licensee cost allocation for taxes, duties and shipping. Given the Licensor hosts and operates the platform through which we receive consolidated market data and transmit orders and trading tickets, no insurance for such a vendor is our walk-away position. We insert a new General Provision (l) at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request). **Fallback offered:** E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

**Termination for convenience (missing).** We are committed to a 36-month initial term (extendable seven years at the Licensor's option) with no convenience right anywhere. The Licensor has no express convenience right either, so the gap is only on our side. We insert Licensee termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination fee as a new clause IV of Article IV. **Fallback:** 60 days' notice.

**Transition assistance and data return (missing).** Article XXI is entirely one-directional: licences cease and we must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information to the Licensor within five days with officer certification. Nothing requires the Licensor to return or export our data or to assist with migration off the hosted trading platform, and the confidentiality return-of-materials language likewise binds only us. We insert a new Article XXI(c): up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter, with survival. **Fallback offered:** 90 days of assistance plus 30-day data export.

---

## 4. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips:

1. **Warranty (Art. VIX)** — AS IS supply with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty or remedy.
2. **Indemnification (Arts. XII–XIII)** — no Vendor IP indemnity, a one-way Customer indemnity, and an express exclusion of Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement.
3. **Limitation of liability (Art. XIII)** — one-way cap and exclusion, Licensor cap below the walk-away floor at one half of amounts paid, our liability unlimited, no carve-outs.
4. **Assignment and change of control (General Provisions; Art. XX)** — blanket Customer assignment ban with no M&A carve-out, plus automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our change of control.

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. Of the nineteen rules assessed, seven clauses are compliant and require no action, eight are deviations requiring redlines, and four rules are unaddressed in the document (insurance, termination for convenience, and post-termination transition assistance / data return).

The Agreement is materially one-sided in the Licensor's favour on the ri[REDACTED] core. Four issues sit in what our playbook treats as walk-away territory and should drive the negotiation:

- **Warranties.** The Licensed Technology is supplied wholly "AS IS" with all express and implied warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty or remedy. The only performance undertaking is a "commercially reasonable efforts" Error Correction obligation in Article VII(f), which is a support commitment rather than a warranty.
- **Indemnities.** The sole indemnity runs from us to the Licensor, and Article XIII expressly excludes all Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims arising from our use of the platform.
- **Limitation of liability.** The cap and the consequential-damages exclusion protect the Licensor only, leaving our liability unlimited and exposed under the broad Article XII indemnity; the Licensor's own cap is set at one half of amounts paid, below our walk-away floor, with no carve-outs.
- **Assignment and change of control.** A blanket one-way ban on our assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, compounded by automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our change of control unless the Licensor consents, with the Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever it believes its interests may be affected.

Secondary but significant: the licence grant excludes our Affiliates and contractors; the Licensor may unilaterally extend the term by a further seven years at its sole option; we have no termination-for-convenience right in a 36-month term; bespoke deliverables we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in the Licensor; and there is no data-return or migration right on exit.

Helpfully, there is **no** exclusivity, no MFN, no minimum volume commitment, no liquidated damages or shortfall charge, and no non-compete binding us. Governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York courts, no arbitration) are at our preferred position.

## 3. Detail on the deviations and gaps

### High severity

**Licence grant scope (deviation).** The Article II grant runs to the Licensee alone, and restriction (e) bars use or access by any individuals other than employees of the Licensee. Affiliates are defined in cl. 1.1 but never brought within the grant, and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded outright; the only route to add them is the Licensor's discretionary prior written consent, which is not the fallback's "affiliates covered on written notice". Our redline extends the grant and restriction (e) to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, with Licensee responsible for their compliance. We note, without separately flagging, that the licence is not revocable at will and that M&A transfer is partially addressed through the Change of Control provision, where consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

**Warranty (deviation).** Article VIX supplies the platform "AS IS" and disclaims all warranties whether express or implied, including merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, accuracy and title, and expressly negates any commitment that errors or non-conformity to the Documentation will be corrected. This is the rule's walk-away position and falls short of even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). We insert a professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, a 12-month conformance-to-Documentation warranty, no-malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranties, and a repair/replace/refund remedy, carved out of the disclaimer. **Fallback offered in comment:** 90-day services / 30-day deliverable warranty.

### Medium severity

**Assignment and change of control (deviation).** One-way blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment, no affiliate or M&A carve-out, no reasonableness standard, and no corresponding restriction on the Licensor. Article XX compounds this with automatic termination of the Agreement and all our licences on our Change of Control absent prior Licensor consent, with the Licensor deemed reasonable in refusing whenever it believes its interests may be adversely affected. Our redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out, makes consent mutual and not unreasonably withheld, bars Licensor assignment to our competitor, and removes the change-of-control termination trigger while retaining notice to the Licensor and the existing definition.

**Vendor indemnity (deviation).** Article XII runs one way only — we indemnify the Licensor for exercise of the licence, the conduct of our business and any breach — and Article XIII excludes all Licensor liability for claims that use of the Licensed Technology infringes third-party IP. **Limitation of liability (deviation).** Article XIII is entirely one-way: both the consequential-damages exclusion and the cap protect the Licensor only, leaving our liability unlimited and exposed under Article XII. The Licensor's cap of one half of amounts paid is below the walk-away floor, and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Our redline makes the exclusion and cap mutual, sets the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, makes Excluded Claims uncapped, and places payment obligations outside the cap. We also note (not separately flagged) the sweeping sentence in (a) disclaiming all Licensor IP-infringement liability.

Redline: 12-month renewals by mutual written agreement, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

**IP ownership (deviation).** Article III vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights in the Licensor, and the definitions of "Intellectual Property Rights" and "Derivative Work" are broad enough that the bespoke client front end and enhancements we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) fall on the Licensor's side. Our only counter-right is a term-limited, non-sublicensable, non-modifiable Field-of-Use licence that ends on termination with all materials returned. There is also no statement that we retain our own trade, order and market data. We do not disturb the Licensor's ownership of its underlying platform; we insert the fallback position (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense paid-for Article VII(b) deliverables) plus an express Licensee Data ownership sentence.

Both the 36-month tail and the all-personnel scope fall in the walk-away band. The general-advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs are already present, so the minimal fix is to make the clause mutual, limit it to individuals directly involved in performance, and cut the tail to 12 months from the end of that involvement.

**Audit (deviation).** Cost allocation is already at our preferred position (Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found), the auditor must be a mutually agreed independent CPA, scope is limited to accounting records, and there is no system-access language. The single failure is the absence of any frequency cap, allowing repeated audits on demand. The 30-day window to permit an audit functions as adequate notice.
